stories.title: India ends Commonwealth Games 2026 with 39 medals and a historic boxing haul — its best-ever Games boxing performance
key_points: India finished **4th overall** at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games with **39 medals**: 13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze.
Indian boxers won **10 medals including 7 golds** — the most golds by any nation in boxing at a single Commonwealth Games ever.
The previous record of **6 golds** was held jointly by England (twice) and Canada — India beat it by one.
India's **para-athletes** had their best Games yet, winning 7 medals — matching the combined tally of all previous editions.
The haul came despite a **reduced program** that excluded medal-rich sports like wrestling, badminton, and hockey.
stories.background: The Commonwealth Games are a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from Commonwealth nations — a lower-profile cousin of the Olympics, but still a major stage for Indian athletes, especially in sports like boxing, wrestling, and weightlifting where India traditionally performs well. This year's Glasgow edition, held July 23 to August 2, notably dropped several sports India usually medals heavily in — wrestling, badminton, table tennis, hockey, and shooting — which made a strong overall tally harder to achieve and puts extra weight on India's performance in the sports that remained.
stories.what_happened: India concluded the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games with **39 medals** — 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze — finishing 4th in the overall standings. Boxing was the standout: Indian boxers won 10 medals including a record **7 golds**, the most golds any country has won in boxing at a single Commonwealth Games, surpassing the previous mark of 6 held by England (at London 1934 and Gold Coast 2018) and matched by Canada at Edinburgh 1986. Gold medals came from Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Arundhati Choudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, Ankush Panghal, and Sakshi Chaudhary, with Jadumani Singh, Lovlina Borgohain, and Narender Berwal taking silver. India's para-athletes also had their best-ever Games, winning 7 medals — 3 gold, 2 silver, 2 bronze — matching the country's combined para medal tally from every previous Commonwealth Games put together.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a genuine record-breaking performance in one of India's traditionally strong Olympic-pipeline sports, achieved despite the Games organizers cutting several sports India usually relies on for medals — which makes the depth of the boxing squad and the growth in para sport especially notable heading toward future Olympic cycles.
stories.ripple_effects: A record boxing haul strengthens the case for continued government and private investment in India's boxing programs ahead of the next Olympic cycle, and the para-sport breakthrough is likely to boost funding and visibility for Indian para-athletes. It also gives several young medalists — many competing at their first major Games — a higher profile heading into future competitions.
stories.why_now: The Games concluded yesterday, August 2, making this the first full accounting of India's final medal tally and the records set along the way.
stories.watch_next: Watch for how the government's Khelo India scheme (funded with a recent ₹36,441 crore push, which we've covered) responds to this result with any new boxing- or para-sport-specific investment.

key_terms.definition: A multi-sport international event held every four years for athletes from Commonwealth nations, seen as a major but slightly lower-tier stage than the Olympics.

stories.the_lesson: A team's medal count alone can hide the real story — comparing performance against a harder, reduced program (fewer sports to medal in) shows whether depth and quality are actually improving, not just whether the raw numbers went up or down.

stories.title: RBI's rate-setting committee begins its 3-day meeting today, with markets betting on a hold at 5.25%
key_points: The RBI's **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meets August 3–5; Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** announces the decision on August 5.
A Reuters poll of 72 economists found **68 expect the repo rate to stay at 5.25%**, only 4 expect a hike, none expect a cut.
The repo rate was last cut by **25 basis points to 5.25%** in December 2025.
The committee is balancing **rising inflation risk** from Gulf oil prices and an uneven monsoon against **strong growth** — SBI Research just raised its Q1 growth estimate to around 7%.
Expect the RBI to keep its policy stance **'neutral'** but strike a more hawkish tone in its commentary.
stories.background: India's central bank, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, sets the country's benchmark interest rate — the **repo rate**, the rate at which it lends to commercial banks — through a six-member Monetary Policy Committee that meets roughly every two months. The RBI's job is to balance keeping inflation in check with supporting economic growth; it cut rates in December 2025 to help growth, and has held steady since. This meeting lands at an unusually complicated moment: the Strait of Hormuz crisis (see our linked story) has kept crude oil prices elevated for months, directly feeding into India's import bill and inflation, while heavy monsoon flooding in Assam, Kerala, and Gujarat adds further uncertainty to food prices and growth.
stories.what_happened: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee began its three-day rate-setting meeting today, August 3, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra due to announce the decision on August 5. A Reuters survey of 72 economists found overwhelming consensus for a hold: 68 expect the repo rate to remain unchanged at **5.25%**, four expect a 25-basis-point hike, and none expect a cut. The committee is weighing elevated crude oil prices — worsened by the ongoing Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions — and monsoon-driven food-price risk against recent strong growth data, with SBI Research raising its Q1 growth estimate to roughly 7% just a day before the meeting began.
stories.why_it_matters: The repo rate influences borrowing costs across the Indian economy — from home loans and business credit to how much the government pays to borrow — so the RBI's decision affects millions of Indians with loans or savings tied to bank interest rates. A hawkish tone alongside a hold would signal the RBI sees inflation risk as serious enough to keep future rate cuts off the table for now.
stories.ripple_effects: If the RBI holds as expected but flags inflation risk from oil prices, banks are likely to keep loan and deposit rates roughly steady in the near term, and equity markets may react more to the tone of the accompanying statement than to the decision itself. A resolution of the Strait of Hormuz crisis (see our linked global story) would ease the oil-price pressure that is the biggest swing factor in this decision.
stories.why_now: The MPC meets on a fixed roughly-bi-monthly schedule, and this cycle happens to fall right as global oil-price risk from the Hormuz crisis and domestic monsoon flooding are both peaking, making this a more closely watched meeting than usual.
stories.watch_next: Watch for Governor Malhotra's policy statement on August 5, especially any change in language around inflation risk and the outlook for future rate moves.

key_terms.definition: The interest rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks — the RBI's main tool for controlling how expensive or cheap borrowing is across the economy.
The six-member RBI committee that meets periodically to set India's benchmark interest rate.

stories.the_lesson: Central banks don't just react to inflation and growth numbers — they react to risk, so an oil-price shock happening on the other side of the world can shape an interest-rate decision that affects loan payments in India, even before it shows up in official inflation data.
stories.market_link: A hold at 5.25% is largely priced in; a hawkish tone could weigh on rate-sensitive sectors like banking, real estate, and autos, while a surprise hike would be more clearly negative for equities and bond prices.

stories.title: Kerala landslides kill 8 as rain traps six fishermen at sea and forces 5,700 into relief camps
key_points: Days of relentless rain have killed **8 people** in Kerala, including **3 children**.
**4 of the 8 deaths** were caused directly by landslides in the state's high-range districts.
**6 fishermen** from Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam remain missing after being swept into the Arabian Sea.
Over **5,700 people** have been moved into relief camps as homes and property sustain heavy damage.
IMD has issued an **orange alert for 12 districts**, warning the intense rain is not yet over.
stories.background: Kerala's steep Western Ghats terrain makes it especially prone to landslides during India's monsoon, when saturated hillsides can give way with little warning, often burying homes downhill. The state has suffered deadly flood and landslide disasters in past monsoon seasons, and disaster-management protocols now include pre-emptive evacuations and fishing bans when heavy rain warnings are issued for coastal and hill districts alike.
stories.what_happened: Kerala has been on high alert since Sunday after days of relentless rain left at least **8 people dead**, including **3 children**, and triggered fresh landslides that claimed **4 lives** in the **Kottayam and Idukki** districts alone. Search operations are continuing for **6 missing fishermen** — four from Thiruvananthapuram and two from Kollam — who went missing in the Arabian Sea, along with **2 Kannur residents** swept away after falling into a river. More than **5,700 people** have been moved to relief camps, with significant damage reported to homes and property across the state's high ranges. The IMD has issued an **orange alert for 12 districts**, warning of continued intense rainfall in the days ahead.
stories.why_it_matters: Landslides are often more lethal than river flooding because they strike with almost no warning, burying homes and people with little chance to evacuate in time — which is why the death toll here is concentrated in hill districts rather than spread evenly across the state.
stories.ripple_effects: Missing fishermen searches divert coast guard and naval resources from other duties; relief-camp displacement disrupts schooling, livelihoods and local economies in affected districts for weeks after the rain stops, and repeated landslide damage raises pressure for stricter hill-slope construction rules.
stories.why_now: An intense, sustained band of monsoon rainfall has been sitting over Kerala's high ranges for several days, saturating hillsides to the point of collapse and pushing coastal fishing conditions into danger territory.
stories.watch_next: Watch for the outcome of the search for the six missing fishermen and whether the IMD's orange alert is upgraded to red for any of the 12 flagged districts.

key_terms.definition: A mountain range running along India's southwestern coast, including Kerala, known for heavy monsoon rainfall and landslide risk.

stories.the_lesson: Landslide risk isn't evenly distributed with rainfall — it concentrates wherever saturated slopes meet human settlement, which is why the same monsoon can be far deadlier in hill districts than in the plains.

stories.title: USA cricketer Akhilesh Reddy banned for eight years over Abu Dhabi T10 match-fixing
key_points: USA international **Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy**, 26, has been banned from all cricket for **eight years**.
The ICC's Anti-Corruption Tribunal found him guilty over conduct during the **2025 Abu Dhabi T10 League**.
He asked a teammate to **'give runs'** — deliberately concede extra runs while bowling — allegedly on behalf of team management.
That teammate refused and instead **reported him to the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit**, and was dropped from the XI as a result.
Reddy also **deleted messages and call logs** from his phone in an attempt to obstruct the investigation.
stories.background: The **Abu Dhabi T10** is a short, fast franchise tournament in the UAE that has repeatedly drawn scrutiny from cricket's anti-corruption authorities, because its **compressed matches, lower player profiles and heavy betting-market interest** make it an attractive target for fixers looking for less scrutiny than bigger leagues get. The **ICC Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU)** monitors global franchise leagues for approaches to players, officials and support staff, and has banned other players and even support-staff members from past T10 editions. Reddy, an Indian-origin American cricketer, was **provisionally suspended in November 2025** while the ICC investigated, and the case has now concluded with a tribunal verdict finding him guilty.
stories.what_happened: The ICC's Anti-Corruption Tribunal found **Akhilesh Reddy** guilty on **three counts** of the Anti-Corruption Code over his conduct during the **2025 Abu Dhabi T10 League**. The tribunal ruled that he approached a teammate — referred to as 'Player A' — and asked him to **'give runs'**, meaning deliberately bowl in a way that concedes extra runs, allegedly at the behest of team management. When that player refused and instead reported the approach to the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit, he was **dropped from the playing XI** shortly before the match in question. Reddy was also found to have **obstructed the investigation** by deleting relevant messages and call logs from his mobile phone once it began. His **eight-year ban is backdated to 21 November 2025**, the date of his provisional suspension, meaning he will not be eligible to return until **2033**.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a case where the player who was approached to fix a match **refused and reported it**, showing cricket's anti-corruption reporting system working as intended instead of a cover-up only being uncovered later. It also reinforces that **smaller, lower-profile franchise leagues** like the Abu Dhabi T10 remain a soft target for match-fixing in global cricket.
stories.ripple_effects: The ban effectively ends Reddy's career with **USA Cricket**, a program trying to build credibility as it grows the sport domestically after co-hosting the 2024 T20 World Cup. It may push tournament organisers and the ICC toward tighter oversight of shorter, lower-salary franchise leagues where the temptation to fix is higher. The tribunal's findings also reference a **'team management'** instruction Reddy says he was acting on, which could mean further action against others is still to come.
stories.why_now: The tribunal's verdict and the eight-year sanction were announced today, closing out an investigation that began with Reddy's **provisional suspension back in November 2025**.
stories.watch_next: Watch whether the ICC's investigation extends further up the chain to the team management Reddy claims directed him, and how USA Cricket responds to a contracted player being banned.

key_terms.definition: The rules that ban cricketers, coaches and officials from fixing matches or parts of matches, or helping others do so, enforced by the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit.
An ultra-short format where each team bats for only 10 overs, so a full match finishes in around 90 minutes.

stories.the_lesson: Corruption in cricket is usually stopped not by outsiders catching a fixer, but by a player on the inside refusing a corrupt approach and reporting it — which is why anti-corruption systems are built around protecting whistle-blowing teammates.

stories.title: Punjab Kings vice-captain Shashank Singh quits Chhattisgarh for Puducherry over 'disrespect'
key_points: Shashank Singh, Punjab Kings' **vice-captain** and the **2023-24 BCCI best domestic white-ball all-rounder**, has left Chhattisgarh for **Puducherry**.
He was dropped from the **2026 Chhattisgarh Cricket Premier League** squad with **no explanation** given.
Singh says the state association gave him **no support** while he recovered from a shoulder injury and a fractured finger.
He will play **white-ball cricket only** this season while he keeps managing his fitness.
The **Chhattisgarh State Cricket Sangh** issued him a **No-Objection Certificate (NOC)** to make the move official.
stories.background: Shashank Singh spent most of a long domestic career representing **Chhattisgarh**, a relatively young state cricket association carved out after the state's 2000 formation, before an explosive **2023 IPL season with Punjab Kings** turned him into a household name and, eventually, the franchise's **vice-captain**. He was named the **BCCI's best domestic white-ball all-rounder for 2023-24**, one of Indian domestic cricket's more prestigious individual honours. Players switch states in Indian domestic cricket occasionally and always need a **No-Objection Certificate (NOC)** from their current association, but a contracted IPL player of Singh's profile walking away is unusual and signals a real breakdown in the player-association relationship, not a routine transfer.
stories.what_happened: Shashank Singh has left **Chhattisgarh** to represent **Puducherry** from the **2026-27 domestic season**, after the Chhattisgarh State Cricket Sangh (CSCS) issued him the NOC he needed to switch states. Singh told ESPNcricinfo the association gave him **no explanation** for excluding him from the **2026 Chhattisgarh Cricket Premier League** squad, and did not tell him why he was also missing from the **conditioning camp** for state probables. He said he had spent much of the past year managing a **shoulder injury and a fractured finger** and felt the board failed to support him through that recovery, adding that someone who won a **BCCI domestic award** deserves 'clarity, not ridicule'. Puducherry has agreed to let him play **white-ball cricket only** for now while he continues managing his fitness. The switch comes only months after Singh was made Punjab Kings' vice-captain in the IPL, raising his public profile just as his domestic-team relationship collapsed.
stories.why_it_matters: It is a rare, public breakdown between a **high-profile IPL player** and his home state association — the kind of selection dispute that usually stays behind closed doors in Indian domestic cricket. It highlights a real tension in the sport: state associations still control **Ranji Trophy and domestic league** selection, but IPL fame increasingly gives players enough leverage and options to simply leave if they feel mismanaged.
stories.ripple_effects: Chhattisgarh cricket loses one of its most recognisable modern players just as its own **Premier League** gets underway, raising uncomfortable questions about how the association manages injured or high-profile players. Puducherry, a smaller domestic side, instantly gains a proven IPL finisher for white-ball cricket. Other contracted IPL players watching a state board criticised in public may feel more confident seeking their own NOCs if they feel unsupported during injury layoffs.
stories.why_now: The move surfaces today because Indian domestic cricket's **2026-27 squad announcements** are being made this week, and Singh's exclusion from the Chhattisgarh Premier League squad was, in his telling, the final straw after months of being ignored by the association.
stories.watch_next: Watch whether the Chhattisgarh association responds publicly to Singh's comments, and whether he is named in a Puducherry white-ball squad in the coming weeks.

key_terms.definition: A formal clearance a player must get from their current state cricket association before they are allowed to represent a different state in Indian domestic cricket.
Cricket played between Indian states and regions, such as the Ranji Trophy, separate from the IPL — it's where most players build their reputation and fitness base.

stories.the_lesson: Even in a sport reshaped by IPL money, a player's week-to-week cricket future still runs through unglamorous state-association decisions — squad lists, fitness camps, medical support — and stardom doesn't exempt anyone from needing that relationship to actually work.

stories.title: Justin Greaves steadies West Indies to 239/5 as spin bowling dominates Day 2 in Trinidad
key_points: West Indies reach **239/5** with **5 wickets in hand** after Day 2
**Justin Greaves** unbeaten on a fighting half-century, an unbroken **66-run stand** with Roston Chase
Pakistan's spin pair **Usman and Sajid** stifled West Indies for long periods
Every West Indies batter reached **double figures** — no cheap wickets for Pakistan
This is the **series-deciding 2nd Test** at Trinidad's Queen's Park Oval
stories.background: Pakistan is touring the West Indies for a **two-match Test series**, with the second and final Test at Trinidad's Queen's Park Oval running **August 2-6**. Day 1 was disrupted by rain and marked by Pakistan's decision to drop veteran fast bowler **Mohammad Abbas**, with West Indies closing on **165 for 3**. Because this is the series decider, every session carries extra weight for both sides.
stories.what_happened: On **Day 2**, West Indies extended their overnight position to **239 for 5** by the time bad light stopped play, taking the upper hand on a spin-dominated day. **Justin Greaves** batted through the innings unbeaten for a fighting half-century, combining with **Roston Chase** for an unbroken **66-run partnership** that pushed the total past 200 with five wickets still in hand. Pakistan's spin duo, **Usman and Sajid**, bowled in tandem for long stretches and kept West Indies pinned down, but couldn't find the breakthroughs they needed — every West Indies batter in the lineup reached double figures, denying Pakistan the cheap dismissals needed to build pressure. Day 1 had already been disrupted by rain, during which Pakistan dropped seasoned pacer Mohammad Abbas from the XI, a call that drew scrutiny given his experience.
stories.why_it_matters: This is the decider in a two-match series, so the runs West Indies are banking now directly shape who wins the series. A modest, grinding total built on 'no cheap wickets' is often more valuable on a tricky, spin-friendly pitch than a flashy but fragile one.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong West Indies total puts pressure on Pakistan's own batting line-up, especially after the selection call to leave out an experienced bowler like Abbas. It also feeds into the ICC World Test Championship standings both sides are trying to climb.
stories.why_now: This is simply the natural progression of the match — Day 2 news follows Day 1, with the series-deciding stakes raising the profile of every session.
stories.watch_next: Watch whether West Indies can extend their lead further on Day 3, and how Pakistan's bowling attack — missing Abbas — copes without their most experienced seamer.
stories.the_lesson: In cricket, disciplined batting that avoids cheap dismissals — even without big, quick scoring — is often what wins low-scoring, series-deciding matches, since it denies the bowling side the wicket clusters that create momentum.

thread.previously: Day 1 was disrupted by rain, and Pakistan's decision to drop experienced seamer Mohammad Abbas drew scrutiny; West Indies closed on 165 for 3.
thread.changed: West Indies extended their position to 239 for 5, with Justin Greaves batting through for an unbeaten half-century and every batter reaching double figures against tight Pakistan spin.

stories.title: BCCI will keep paying Ajinkya Rahane a ₹70,000 monthly pension even after his retirement
key_points: Rahane qualifies for BCCI's **elite pension scheme** after playing **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is** for India
He'll receive **₹70,000 a month** under the board's **2022-revised pension scheme**, up from ₹50,000 previously
The pension gets **suspended** if he takes a full-time BCCI role like coach or selector — but can resume if he later leaves that role
This follows his retirement from all international cricket, announced **July 30**
stories.background: The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) runs a **pension scheme for former international players** who meet career-length thresholds, as a form of long-term financial security once players stop earning central contracts and match fees. The scheme was **revised upward in 2022**, raising payouts for senior former players. Rahane retired from all formats of international cricket on **July 30, 2026** — a career that included being the hero of India's historic **2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy win in Australia**, widely seen as one of Indian cricket's greatest overseas triumphs.
stories.what_happened: Days after Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from all international cricket, it's been confirmed he qualifies for the BCCI's **elite player pension scheme**, thanks to a long international career spanning **85 Tests, 90 ODIs, and 20 T20Is**. Under the board's **2022-revised pension structure**, he'll receive **₹70,000 per month** — up from the ₹50,000 top-tier former players received under the earlier scheme. There is one condition: if Rahane takes on a **full-time BCCI role**, such as a national or state coaching position or a selector's post, the monthly pension will be **temporarily suspended** for as long as he holds that job, and can resume once he leaves it.
stories.why_it_matters: The pension underscores how the BCCI, easily the world's wealthiest cricket board, has formalized long-term financial support for former internationals — a benefit far less common in cricket boards elsewhere in the world.
stories.ripple_effects: It reinforces the financial security net now available to India's senior retired cricketers, and may factor into other veteran players' retirement timing decisions. It also raises the question of whether Rahane will pursue a coaching or selection role next, which would pause the payments.
stories.why_now: This detail is emerging now as follow-up coverage to Rahane's retirement announcement on July 30, once outlets dug into what his benefits package actually looks like.
stories.watch_next: Watch for any announcement of a post-retirement coaching, mentorship, or selection role for Rahane, which would trigger the pension suspension clause.

key_terms.definition: A monthly payment the Board of Control for Cricket in India gives to former international players who meet career-length thresholds, as long-term financial support after retirement.

stories.title: Ben Duckett becomes The Hundred's leading run-scorer as Trent Rockets edge SunRisers Leeds
key_points: **Trent Rockets** beat **SunRisers Leeds** by **5 runs** at Trent Bridge to stay top of the Men's Hundred table.
**Ben Duckett** smashed **64** off 47 balls, overtaking Phil Salt to become the competition's **leading run-scorer**.
**Aneurin Donald**, playing his first game of the tournament, blitzed a 19-ball **40 not out** with three sixes.
Pakistan pace veteran **Mohammad Amir** took 2 wickets for 20 runs in the death overs to seal the win.
Harry Brook fell for 46, caught by Duckett himself, as SunRisers fell 5 runs short chasing 147.
stories.background: The Hundred splits each match into 100-ball innings rather than the usual 120-ball T20 format, rewarding explosive hitting and tight death bowling. **Trent Rockets** have been one of the standout men's teams this season, and this was their third successive win, while **SunRisers Leeds**, led by Australian all-rounder Mitchell Marsh, came into the game looking to keep pace near the top of the table.
stories.what_happened: Batting first, Trent Rockets got a rapid start from **Aneurin Donald**, playing his first match of the campaign, who smashed **40 not out** off just 19 balls including three sixes. **Ben Duckett** then took over, reaching his third half-century of the tournament from 35 balls and adding a 50-run stand with Tim David before falling for **64** — a knock that made him the competition's leading run-scorer, overtaking England team-mate Phil Salt. Rockets posted **146 for 4**. In reply, Mitchell Marsh and Zak Crawley gave SunRisers Leeds a solid start, reaching 32 for 1 after the powerplay. Harry Brook threatened to take the game away before being caught by Duckett off Mohammad Amir for 46. Amir then struck twice more in the death overs, finishing with **2 for 20**, as SunRisers fell 5 runs short on **141 for 4**.
stories.why_it_matters: This result keeps Trent Rockets at the top of the men's table heading into the closing stages of the group phase, while individual milestones like Duckett's run-scoring lead feed into conversations about England white-ball selection and player value in franchise leagues worldwide.
stories.ripple_effects: Trent Rockets strengthen their claim to a top finish and a home knockout match, while SunRisers Leeds slip further off the pace despite Marsh and Brook's form. Duckett's red-hot Hundred form adds to the selection conversation around England's white-ball top order.
stories.why_now: The match was played on August 2, with reaction and reports still fresh as the tournament heads into its final week.
stories.watch_next: Watch whether Trent Rockets can maintain their unbeaten run and hold off SunRisers Leeds and other challengers as the race for the knockout stages tightens.

The final overs of a limited-overs innings, when bowlers try to defend a small target and batters try to maximize scoring.
The league standings that rank teams by wins, used to decide who reaches the knockout stage.

stories.the_lesson: In short-format cricket, a couple of quickfire cameos at the top of the order plus tight death bowling are often enough to win a game — and individual form in these leagues increasingly shapes international team selection.

stories.title: England's Danni Wyatt-Hodge ruled out of the rest of The Hundred with a calf tear
key_points: MI London's **Danni Wyatt-Hodge** ruled out of the remainder of the **Women's Hundred 2026** with a torn left calf.
The injury happened while she batted through pain for an unbeaten **52** against Southern Brave on July 27.
**Ella Claridge**, a 23-year-old USA international, has been signed as her replacement.
Wyatt-Hodge was MI London's joint-top run-scorer this season with **93 runs** at a strike rate of **132.85**.
MI London remain **winless** at the bottom of the table, now without one of their most in-form batters.
stories.background: The Hundred is England's short-format cricket competition where each team faces 100 balls per innings instead of the usual 120 in a T20. Danni Wyatt-Hodge is a veteran England international opening batter with over a decade of white-ball experience for her country. She plays for **MI London**, one of eight teams in the competition, who have struggled all season and sit **last** in the standings without a win. Losing an experienced international mid-season is a significant blow for a side already searching for answers.
stories.what_happened: Wyatt-Hodge picked up the injury while playing through discomfort during MI London's narrow loss to Southern Brave, where she still top-scored with an unbeaten **52**. Scans have since confirmed a **left calf tear**, ruling her out for the rest of the tournament. The Hundred has confirmed **Ella Claridge**, a 23-year-old batter who plays for the USA internationally and for The Blaze domestically, as her replacement in the MI London squad. The news follows fellow captain **Sophie Devine's** calf injury elsewhere in the competition, meaning two teams have lost key top-order batters to the same type of injury within days of each other. Wyatt-Hodge's 93 runs this season, at an average of 46.50, had made her one of the few bright spots in an otherwise winless campaign for MI London.
stories.why_it_matters: Losing a proven international batter mid-tournament forces a struggling team to rebuild its top order on the fly, right when it most needs experienced runs. It also underlines how the packed modern cricket calendar — leagues stacked back-to-back with international duty — is producing a steady stream of soft-tissue injuries like calf and hamstring tears.
stories.ripple_effects: MI London, already winless, must now find fresh runs at the top of the order from Ella Claridge, a new face in the competition, while chasing their first win of the season. For Claridge, it's a high-profile opportunity in one of the world's most-watched T20 leagues. The injury also adds to a growing list of niggles this Hundred season.
stories.why_now: The Hundred confirmed the scan results and Claridge's signing on August 3, making this the freshest team-news development in the tournament.
stories.watch_next: Watch how Ella Claridge performs on her MI London debut and whether the team can find its first win of the season without Wyatt-Hodge.

stories.title: Rashid Khan claims his maiden Hundred five-wicket haul as MI London thump Manchester Super Giants Men
key_points: **Rashid Khan** took a career-first **5 for 17** in the Men's Hundred, dismantling Manchester Super Giants
**MI London** won by **45 runs**, posting 183/6 (Jacks 62, Pooran 54) before bowling MSG out for 138
**Aiden Markham's 50** was the lone resistance as Rashid ran through the rest of the batting order
The win lifts **MI London to second place** in the men's competition table
stories.background: The Hundred is England's 100-balls-per-innings franchise tournament, running men's and women's competitions in parallel each August. Rashid Khan is one of world cricket's most respected leg-spinners, a veteran of franchise leagues worldwide, but had never previously taken a five-wicket haul in this specific competition despite years of taking wickets in it.
stories.what_happened: MI London posted 183 for 6, built around fifties from **Will Jacks (62)** and **Nicholas Pooran (54)**, at their home ground. In reply, Manchester Super Giants Men were bowled out for 138, with Rashid Khan tearing through their middle and lower order to finish with figures of 5 for 17 — his best-ever return in the tournament. **Aiden Markham's 50** was the only substantial score MSG could muster as they slipped to a 45-run defeat. The win moves MI London up to second place in the men's points table as the group stage heads toward its business end.
stories.why_it_matters: It's a big momentum boost for MI London's playoff push and a reminder that Rashid Khan, despite years in franchise cricket, can still produce a career-best performance on his day.
stories.ripple_effects: The result reshuffles the points table with the group stage nearing completion, strengthening MI London's playoff position while denting Manchester Super Giants' own hopes.
stories.why_now: The match was played on Sunday, August 2, as part of the tournament's regular group-stage schedule.
stories.watch_next: MI London's remaining group games as the table tightens before the playoffs.
stories.the_lesson: In short-format cricket, one bowler having a career-best day can single-handedly decide a match — collective depth matters less than an individual bursting into peak form at the right moment.

stories.title: India shakes up its coaching staff for the Sri Lanka Tests, naming a new fielding coach and losing an assistant to the IPL
key_points: BCCI appointed **Subhadeep Ghosh** as India men's new fielding coach ahead of the Sri Lanka Tests.
Ghosh, 57, from **Assam**, replaces **T Dilip** in the role.
He previously coached the **India women's team** for two years, including at two World Cups.
Assistant coach **Ryan ten Doeschate** has left to join **Kolkata Knight Riders** as Head of Cricket Strategy.
The changes land just before India's **two-Test series in Sri Lanka**, starting August 15 in Galle.
stories.background: India's tour of Sri Lanka is an important early assignment for **Shubman Gill's** side in the current World Test Championship cycle, and it comes as the team is already dealing with a personnel setback — pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out of the series with a knee injury. Coaching staff changes like this one are less visible than playing XI news but shape how the team prepares and performs, and India's franchise T20 league, the IPL, regularly recruits national-team support staff — as it has here with ten Doeschate.
stories.what_happened: The BCCI announced on Monday that **Subhadeep Ghosh**, a 57-year-old former Assam and Railways cricketer from Digboi, has been appointed India men's new fielding coach, replacing **T Dilip**, ahead of the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka. Ghosh previously spent two years coaching the **India women's team**, and was part of the support staff during the **2022 Women's ODI World Cup** and the **2023 Women's T20 World Cup**. As a player, he represented Assam and Railways in 17 first-class and 17 List A matches. Separately, assistant coach **Ryan ten Doeschate** has left the India setup to join the **Kolkata Knight Riders** as Head of Cricket Strategy, an IPL role.
stories.why_it_matters: Fielding standards and support-staff continuity directly affect on-field results, and this reshuffle happens right before a significant overseas Test series where India is already missing its premier fast bowler — making the new coaching team's first assignment a high-stakes one.
stories.ripple_effects: Ghosh's appointment also signals a pathway from the women's team setup into the men's senior team's coaching staff, while ten Doeschate's move to KKR is another example of IPL franchises drawing experienced staff away from national team roles.
stories.why_now: The appointment comes just ahead of the squad's departure for Sri Lanka, timed to have the new fielding coach in place before the series begins on August 15.
stories.watch_next: How the new-look coaching staff performs when the two-Test series against Sri Lanka begins in Galle on August 15.
stories.the_lesson: Behind every playing XI is a coaching staff whose changes rarely make headlines but can matter just as much — continuity and specialist expertise in areas like fielding compound over a long tour.

stories.title: England captain Sophie Devine ruled out for the rest of The Hundred 2026 with a calf injury
key_points: **Sophie Devine**, Welsh Fire's captain, is **out for the rest of The Hundred 2026** with a calf injury.
She was hurt attempting a catch during Welsh Fire's loss to **Birmingham Phoenix** on Saturday.
Ireland all-rounder **Orla Prendergast** replaces her in the squad.
Australian leg-spinner **Georgia Wareham** takes over as **Welsh Fire captain** for the rest of the season.
The injury is a blow for Welsh Fire, who lose both their **captain and a senior batter** mid-tournament.
stories.background: **The Hundred** is England's short-form domestic cricket competition, played in 100-ball innings rather than the more traditional 20-over (120-ball) format, and it runs as parallel men's and women's tournaments each August. Teams are packed with a mix of English internationals and star overseas players signed for just this one tournament, so a single injury to a captain or senior player can significantly reshape a team's season, since replacements are drawn from a smaller reserve pool than in international cricket. **Sophie Devine**, a veteran New Zealand international, has been one of the most consistent all-format players in women's cricket and was leading **Welsh Fire** this season.
stories.what_happened: **Sophie Devine** injured her calf while attempting to take a catch early in Birmingham Phoenix's run chase during Welsh Fire's defeat on Saturday, and she spent the rest of that match off the field. She has now been **ruled out for the remainder of The Hundred 2026**. Ireland all-rounder **Orla Prendergast** has been named as her replacement in the Welsh Fire squad and was available for the team's following fixture against Southern Brave. With Devine unavailable, Australian leg-spinner **Georgia Wareham** has taken over as **Welsh Fire's captain** for the rest of the competition.
stories.why_it_matters: Losing a captain and senior all-rounder mid-tournament is a significant setback for Welsh Fire's campaign, and it reshuffles both the team's leadership and its batting/bowling balance for the remaining matches. It's also a reminder of how injury-prone short, intense franchise tournaments can be for players who shuttle between multiple competitions around the world with little recovery time.
stories.ripple_effects: Expect Welsh Fire's results and team balance to shift under Wareham's captaincy, and for Prendergast's form to become a talking point as she steps into a bigger role than originally planned. It also adds Devine to a growing list of players sidelined by injury during this year's Hundred, alongside other players managing knocks across the competition.
stories.why_now: The injury happened Saturday and the season-ending diagnosis was confirmed and reported over the following days, making this a fresh development in the ongoing tournament.
stories.watch_next: Watch how Welsh Fire perform under Georgia Wareham's captaincy in their remaining group-stage matches, and whether they can still make a playoff push.

stories.the_lesson: Crowded global franchise cricket calendars mean players are almost always managing fatigue or minor injuries — a single awkward catch attempt can end a star player's tournament and force teams to promote reserves into much bigger roles than planned.

stories.title: Rain and Mohammad Abbas's shock axing shape Day 1 as West Indies close on 165/3 in the series-deciding 2nd Test
key_points: West Indies closed Day 1 on **165/3** at the **Queen's Park Oval, Port of Spain**, with **Shai Hope and Justin Greaves** counterattacking late.
Only **9.5 overs** were possible before an early, rain-forced lunch, with West Indies at **49/1** at the break.
Pakistan's **shock decision to omit pacer Mohammad Abbas** was the pre-match talking point, with spinners **Ali Usman and Sajid Khan** bowling 25 of the day's overs instead.
West Indies arrive **1-0 up** in the two-match series after a **90-run win** in the opener, meaning this Test decides the series.
The pitch is shaping up as **spin-dominant**, a shift from the pace-friendly conditions of the first Test.
stories.background: **Pakistan** came into this tour after already losing the **series opener by 90 runs** at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy, meaning they had to win this second and final Test in **Port of Spain, Trinidad** just to level the series — any other result and **West Indies win the series**. The **Queen's Park Oval** is historically one of the more spin-friendly venues in the Caribbean, which shaped both sides' team selection, most notably Pakistan's decision to leave out a frontline pace bowler.
stories.what_happened: Rain repeatedly disrupted play on Day 1 of the series-deciding second Test between **West Indies and Pakistan** at the Queen's Park Oval — only **9.5 overs** were bowled before an early lunch forced by rain, with West Indies **49/1** at that point. Pakistan's bowling was built around spin rather than pace after the team made the **surprise call to leave out fast bowler Mohammad Abbas**; spinners **Ali Usman and Sajid Khan** bowled a combined **25 overs** and took two of the three wickets to fall. **Shai Hope and Justin Greaves** counterattacked in the last 45 minutes of play, pushing West Indies to **165/3** by the close, with Greaves unbeaten on 52. West Indies, who won the series opener by 90 runs, need only a draw or win here to take the series; Pakistan must win to level it.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a series decider — West Indies can wrap up a series win from here, while Pakistan face a must-win Test on a pitch that appears to be turning against their strength (they left out their frontline seamer).
stories.ripple_effects: A West Indies series win would extend a strong recent home run for the team and add pressure on Pakistan's team management over the Abbas selection call; a Pakistan comeback would keep alive a tense series storyline through the final days.
stories.why_now: Day 1 of the Test was played on August 2, with rain interruptions and the Abbas omission both shaping how the day unfolded — the close-of-play position sets up the rest of the match.
stories.watch_next: Watch how the pitch behaves on Day 2 — if it keeps turning as expected, Pakistan's spin-heavy attack could either pay off or expose their thinner pace options.
stories.the_lesson: In cricket, a single bold selection call — like dropping a frontline bowler — can shape an entire Test's tactics and become the storyline of the match regardless of the final result.

stories.title: Beth Mooney powers Trent Rockets Women past Welsh Fire in Cardiff for a second Hundred win

stories.title: Auqib Nabi set to replace the injured Bumrah in India's Test squad for Sri Lanka

thread.previously: We reported Jasprit Bumrah had been ruled out of India's upcoming two-Test series in Sri Lanka after failing to recover from a left knee injury picked up during the England ODI series.
thread.changed: India now has a named replacement: Jammu & Kashmir pace-bowling all-rounder Auqib Nabi is set to be drafted into the squad in Bumrah's place.

key_points: **Auqib Nabi** is set to replace Jasprit Bumrah in India's Test squad for Sri Lanka.
Nabi has taken **100-plus wickets** across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons for Jammu & Kashmir.
He was the **chief architect** of J&K's red-ball success in domestic cricket.
Bumrah's knee injury, from the England ODI series, hasn't healed enough for him to bowl.
India's squad is set to arrive in Sri Lanka on **August 4**, with the first Test starting **August 15 in Galle**.
stories.background: Jasprit Bumrah, India's premier fast bowler, picked up a left knee injury while fielding during the ODI series in England and had been undergoing rehabilitation at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru. Despite reports he had passed some fitness tests, he had not resumed bowling, and the medical team judged he needed more time rather than risk aggravating the injury — leading to his exclusion from the two-Test tour of Sri Lanka. That left a spot open in India's fast-bowling attack for the series.
stories.what_happened: BCCI sources indicate **Auqib Nabi**, a seam-bowling all-rounder from Jammu & Kashmir, is set to be added to India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour as Bumrah's replacement. Nabi has picked up more than 100 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons and was central to J&K's recent red-ball success domestically, making him a rewarded, form-based pick rather than a like-for-like swap for Bumrah's pace and experience. India's squad is scheduled to arrive in Sri Lanka on August 4, ahead of the first of two Tests starting August 15 in Galle, with the second in Colombo on August 23.
stories.why_it_matters: Losing Bumrah for any Test series is a significant blow to India's attack — he is widely regarded as one of the world's best fast bowlers — so the composition of his replacement shapes how India's bowling unit is likely to perform in Sri Lankan conditions. Nabi's call-up is also a notable opportunity for a domestic-cricket performer to step onto the international stage.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong showing from Nabi in Sri Lanka could accelerate his path into India's broader fast-bowling pool for future series, while Bumrah's continued absence keeps the spotlight on his fitness ahead of India's busier international calendar later in the year.
stories.why_now: The replacement is being finalised now because the squad departs for Sri Lanka on August 4, forcing selectors to lock in the touring party this week.
stories.watch_next: Official confirmation of the squad from the BCCI, and how Nabi performs if given a Test debut in Galle.

stories.the_lesson: Injuries to star players create openings, but who gets picked to fill them usually comes down to consistent domestic performance — a reminder that international careers are often built on years of unglamorous, lower-profile cricket.

stories.title: Rain washes out Jaffna Kings' LPL clash, eliminating Dambulla Sixers and confirming the four playoff teams

thread.previously: We noted that table-topping Jaffna Kings, already through to the playoffs, were set to face bottom-placed Dambulla Sixers as the Lanka Premier League's group stage wrapped up.
thread.changed: That match never finished: persistent rain in Pallekele washed it out after Dambulla Sixers batted, meaning the points were shared and **Dambulla Sixers were eliminated**, while the LPL 2026 playoff lineup is now officially confirmed.

key_points: Dambulla Sixers posted **203/8** batting first, but Jaffna Kings never got to bat as rain **abandoned the match**.
**Pavan Rathnayake (47)** and **Dinesh Chandimal (44)** led Dambulla's innings before the washout.
With points shared, **Dambulla Sixers are eliminated** from the LPL 2026 playoff race.
The confirmed **playoff four** are Galle Gallants, Jaffna Kings, Colombo Kaps, and Kandy Royals.
The result closes out the LPL 2026 group stage after 20 matches.
stories.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's franchise T20 cricket tournament, run alongside other domestic leagues each year. Going into this match, Jaffna Kings had already secured a playoff spot as group leaders, while Dambulla Sixers sat bottom of the table and needed a win — and help elsewhere — just to have a chance of qualifying, making this final group-stage fixture effectively a knockout match for Dambulla even though Jaffna's own position was already safe.
stories.what_happened: Dambulla Sixers, batting first at Pallekele International Cricket Stadium, posted 203 for 8 in their 20 overs, with Pavan Rathnayake top-scoring on 47 off 28 balls and Dinesh Chandimal adding a quick 44 off 24. But persistent rain delayed the start of Jaffna Kings' chase and eventually forced match officials to abandon the game entirely, without Jaffna facing a single ball. Under the tournament's rules, the abandoned match meant points were shared between the two sides — enough to confirm Dambulla Sixers' elimination from playoff contention, while Galle Gallants, Jaffna Kings, Colombo Kaps, and Kandy Royals are the four teams through to the LPL 2026 playoffs.
stories.why_it_matters: This closes out the LPL 2026 group stage and sets the confirmed final-four lineup for the playoffs, which now become the tournament's remaining storyline — and it's a reminder of how weather, not just performance on the field, can decide a team's season in T20 franchise cricket.
stories.ripple_effects: Dambulla Sixers' season ends here, while the four confirmed playoff teams now shift focus to squad and strategy planning for the knockout rounds. Broadcasters and sponsors also get clarity on which teams and players will feature in the more closely watched playoff matches.
stories.why_now: The match was the final fixture of the LPL 2026 group stage, so its outcome — even an incomplete, rain-affected one — was always going to decide the last playoff spot.
stories.watch_next: Watch for the LPL 2026 playoff schedule and fixtures involving Galle Gallants, Jaffna Kings, Colombo Kaps, and Kandy Royals.
stories.the_lesson: In T20 tournaments with shared-points rules for abandoned matches, a team can be eliminated without ever getting the chance to actually play for a result — the rulebook itself can decide a season, not just what happens on the field.

stories.title: Mumbai Indians publicly deny CSK trade talks over Hardik Pandya, calling reports 'contrary' to fact

thread.previously: We reported that Chennai Super Kings had joined the race for Hardik Pandya, with reports saying up to seven IPL franchises now wanted him, and that CSK were reportedly prepared to offer cash plus a player swap.
thread.changed: Mumbai Indians has now **officially denied** being in trade talks with CSK or anyone else, saying its post-season review isn't even finished yet — directly contradicting the specific swap terms (Shivam Dube, Ayush Mhatre, and cash) that had been widely reported.

key_points: A Mumbai Indians spokesperson said: **'we are not engaged in conversations regarding player trades.'**
MI says any trade decision can only happen **after its post-season review is complete**.
Reports had claimed MI wanted **Shivam Dube and Ayush Mhatre** from CSK in exchange for Hardik Pandya.
Pandya's IPL 2026 season was poor: **206 runs at 22.89**, no fifties, and an economy rate of 11.43 with the ball.
Mumbai Indians **missed the IPL 2026 playoffs**, fueling scrutiny of Pandya's captaincy.
stories.background: Hardik Pandya has captained Mumbai Indians since returning to the franchise in 2024, but the team has struggled since, missing the IPL 2026 playoffs entirely — a poor result that has put his captaincy and place in the squad under public scrutiny. Speculation about a trade to Chennai Super Kings (CSK), the franchise he started his career away from, built through late July and into this week, with multiple reports naming specific players CSK might offer in exchange, even though neither franchise had confirmed anything officially.
stories.what_happened: A Mumbai Indians spokesperson pushed back directly on days of trade speculation, saying: 'Contrary to reports, we are not engaged in conversations regarding player trades; any trade would only be possible once the review is complete.' This contradicts specific reports from earlier this week claiming MI wanted CSK's Shivam Dube and Ayush Mhatre in exchange for handing over Pandya, with CSK reportedly offering Dube, Dewald Brevis, and roughly ₹10 crore in cash as an alternative package. The speculation had been fueled by Pandya's weak IPL 2026 numbers — just 206 runs at an average of 22.89 with no half-centuries, and an economy rate of 11.43 with the ball — alongside Mumbai Indians' failure to make the playoffs.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a real check on a trade story that had built significant momentum in the press — MI's direct denial means fans and other franchises (Delhi Capitals, KKR, and Rajasthan Royals were reportedly also watching) should treat the specific swap terms reported so far as unconfirmed rumor rather than an imminent deal.
stories.ripple_effects: If MI genuinely hasn't started trade talks, CSK and other interested franchises may need to wait for Mumbai's official post-season review before any real negotiation can happen, likely pushing any potential move closer to the IPL 2027 auction window. It also keeps Pandya's captaincy status at Mumbai Indians an open question heading into the off-season.
stories.why_now: The denial comes today, directly responding to a wave of trade reports that had built up over the past two days, making this the latest concrete data point in an active, fast-moving transfer saga.
stories.watch_next: Watch for whether Mumbai Indians completes its post-season review and whether any official trade talks are confirmed by either franchise afterward.
stories.the_lesson: In sports transfer sagas, specific-sounding details (named players, exact cash figures) can spread through media reports well before either party confirms anything — an official denial from one side is a reminder that 'reports say' is not the same as a real deal.

stories.title: Ajinkya Rahane, hero of India's historic 2020-21 Australia comeback, retires from all cricket
key_points: Rahane retires from **international and all formats** after a **17-year** career.
He played **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is**, plus **212 IPL matches** across six franchises.
He is best remembered for captaining India to a stunning series win in Australia in **2020-21**, with regular captain Virat Kohli away.
His last international appearance was a **Test in the West Indies in July 2023**.
He last played competitively in **IPL 2026**, captaining Kolkata Knight Riders to **335 runs in 14 matches**.
stories.background: Ajinkya Rahane built his reputation as one of Indian cricket's most reliable overseas Test batters, prized for gritty, patient innings in tough conditions rather than flashy stroke-play. His defining moment came during India's **2020-21 tour of Australia**, when he took over the Test captaincy after Virat Kohli returned home for the birth of his child — and led a weakened, injury-hit Indian side to a historic series win at the **Gabba in Brisbane**, a ground Australia had not lost at in over 30 years. He had not played for India since mid-2023, with his career since then largely continuing through franchise T20 cricket.
stories.what_happened: Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from **international cricket and all formats**, closing out a career spanning more than **17 years**. In an emotional video message, he said: **"I have always relied on timing in my batting and I have always understood its importance. Today, I feel the timing is right for me to move on."** Across his career he played **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is** for India, plus **212 IPL matches** for six different franchises. His last India appearance came in a **Test match in the West Indies in July 2023**. He continued playing in the IPL afterward, most recently captaining **Kolkata Knight Riders** in the 2026 season, where he scored **335 runs in 14 matches** at age 38.
stories.why_it_matters: Rahane's retirement closes the book on one of the last active members of India's dominant 2010s-2020s Test batting core, and formally ends the international career of the man who delivered one of Indian cricket's most celebrated away series wins.
stories.ripple_effects: His exit opens up conversation about India's next generation of overseas-conditions Test specialists, and frees up an IPL captaincy slot at Kolkata Knight Riders ahead of the next auction cycle.
stories.why_now: At 38 and without international selection since 2023, Rahane's announcement follows a now-common pattern of senior Indian cricketers formally retiring once their competitive IPL involvement also winds down, rather than fading out quietly.
stories.watch_next: Watch for tributes from teammates and the BCCI, and how Kolkata Knight Riders plan their captaincy going into the next IPL auction cycle.

key_terms.definition: The Test series played between India and Australia, named after two legendary former captains of each side.

stories.the_lesson: In sport, a career's legacy is often defined by a single, high-pressure moment rather than career-long statistics — Rahane will be remembered first for one series win, even though his career spanned 17 years and hundreds of matches.

stories.title: Chennai Super Kings join the race for Hardik Pandya as reports say seven IPL franchises now want him
key_points: **Chennai Super Kings (CSK)** have become the latest IPL team to chase all-rounder **Hardik Pandya**.
Reports say as many as **seven IPL franchises** are now interested in signing him.
Mumbai Indians (MI) officially deny any trade talks are happening **at this stage**.
MI are conducting a **full end-of-season review** after a disappointing IPL 2026 campaign before deciding.
**Rohit Sharma** could be handed the MI captaincy again if Pandya does leave.

stories.title: Sophie Ecclestone rips through MI London's top order as Manchester Super Giants Women keep winless MI London bottom of The Hundred
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants Women** beat **MI London Women** by **6 wickets**, with 28 balls to spare, at The Oval.
England spinner **Sophie Ecclestone**, opening the bowling for the first time this season, took out both openers cheaply and was named **Player of the Match**.
MI London were bowled out for just **92**, having also been without star player **Danni Wyatt-Hodge**.
Manchester chased the target down comfortably, reaching **95/4**.
The result leaves **MI London still winless** and rooted to the **bottom of the table** in this year's Hundred Women's Competition.
stories.background: The Hundred is England's 100-ball cricket franchise competition, running men's and women's tournaments in parallel each summer since 2021, and has become a key summer showcase for both international and domestic women's talent. **Sophie Ecclestone** is one of the world's best left-arm spin bowlers and a regular fixture for England, making her performances a headline draw whenever she plays. MI London have struggled all season and came into this match already at the bottom of the points table, still searching for their first win.
stories.what_happened: At **The Oval** in London, MI London Women won the toss, chose to bat, and collapsed to just **92 all out**, playing without regular player Danni Wyatt-Hodge. **Sophie Ecclestone**, bowling the opening spell of the innings for the first time this season, struck twice early — dismissing both Alice Davidson-Richards and Hayley Matthews — to leave MI London reeling at 1 for 2, before finishing a tight spell conceding just **7 runs off 20 balls**. In reply, **Manchester Super Giants Women** chased the target down comfortably, reaching **95/4** with 28 balls remaining to win by **6 wickets**. Ecclestone was named Player of the Match for her spell.
stories.why_it_matters: The win boosts Manchester Super Giants' net run rate and playoff positioning, while MI London's continued winless run leaves them facing an increasingly difficult path back into contention this season.
stories.ripple_effects: MI London will likely make squad or tactical changes ahead of their remaining fixtures to try to arrest the slide, while Manchester's bowling depth — now spearheaded by an in-form Ecclestone — makes them a tougher out for the rest of the competition.
stories.why_now: The match was played and completed today as part of the ongoing 2026 Hundred Women's Competition season, which runs until mid-August.
stories.watch_next: Watch MI London's next fixture for signs of a lineup change as they continue searching for their first win of the season.

key_terms.definition: A shortened cricket format where each team bats for 100 balls instead of the usual 120 (20 six-ball overs), designed to be quicker and more TV-friendly.

stories.the_lesson: In short-format cricket, one devastating opening spell can decide a match before it's even a third of the way through — early wickets compound fast because there are so few balls left to recover.

stories.title: Argentina Women beat Canada Women to go 3-0 up in a rare cricket series in South America
key_points: Argentina defended a modest **96/9** to bowl Canada out for **78**, winning by **18 runs**.
**Alina Emch** was player of the match, scoring 17 off 18 balls then taking **3 wickets for 16 runs**.
The win gives Argentina an **unassailable 3-0 lead** in a seven-match T20I series.
Argentina had already won the series opener by a dramatic **1 wicket** on July 29.
The series is being played in **Buenos Aires**, a country with almost no cricketing tradition.
stories.background: Cricket is a minor sport in South America, where football dominates, but the International Cricket Council (ICC) has been funding development in 'associate' nations — countries without full Test status — to grow the game's global footprint. Argentina and Canada are both ICC associate members building up their national teams ahead of qualifying tournaments for global events like the Women's T20 World Cup. This series, played on Argentina's home turf, is part of that development effort.
stories.what_happened: Argentina Women, captained by **Maria Castiñeiras**, defended a total of just **96/9** to beat Canada Women (captained by Rabbjyot Rajput) by **18 runs** in the 4th T20I of a seven-match series, bowling Canada out for **78** in 18.4 overs. Player of the match **Alina Emch** top-scored for Argentina with **17 off 18 balls** and then took **3 wickets for 16 runs** with the ball. It was Argentina's third straight win, giving them an unassailable **3-0 series lead** — they had already won the opener on July 29 by a dramatic 1 wicket, with Julia Andujar and Francesca Galan steering the chase home. Two more matches were scheduled for August 2 itself.
stories.why_it_matters: A team from a country with virtually no cricket history winning consistently against a fellow associate nation is a genuine marker of the sport's slow expansion beyond its traditional strongholds in South Asia, England, and Australia.
stories.ripple_effects: Continued success could help Argentina secure more ICC development funding and fixtures, and builds a small domestic fan base and player pathway in a country where cricket has essentially no professional infrastructure. It's also a data point for the broader push toward more competitive Women's T20 World Cup qualifying rounds.
stories.why_now: The result landed yesterday, August 1, as part of an ongoing series, with the series lead now decided ahead of the final two matches today.
stories.watch_next: The outcome of the final two matches of the series, played today, August 2, and whether Argentina completes a series whitewash.

key_terms.definition: A cricket-playing nation that hasn't been granted full 'Test' status — associate teams like Argentina and Canada compete in a separate development pathway toward global tournaments.

stories.the_lesson: Sports expand into new markets slowly and unevenly — a single dramatic series win in a non-traditional country is a small signal, not proof, that a sport is truly taking root there.

stories.title: Trent Rockets Women edge Sunrisers Leeds Women by 5 runs in The Hundred
key_points: Trent Rockets Women posted **139/7** from their 100 balls at Trent Bridge, Nottingham.
Sunrisers Leeds Women fell **5 runs short**, finishing on 134/5.
**Annabel Sutherland** anchored the chase for Leeds with an unbeaten innings that ultimately wasn't enough.
The result is part of Match 17 of the **2026 Hundred Women's Competition** group stage.
stories.background: **The Hundred** is England's short-form cricket franchise competition — eight men's and eight women's teams, each city-based, playing a 100-ball-per-innings format designed to be faster and more TV-friendly than a normal T20. Trent Rockets and Sunrisers Leeds are two of the competition's franchises, based in Nottingham and Leeds respectively, and this fixture was the 17th match of the 2026 season's group stage.
stories.what_happened: Batting first at Trent Bridge, Trent Rockets Women set a target of 140 from their 100 balls. Sunrisers Leeds Women's chase was built around a fighting innings from **Annabel Sutherland**, but the required rate crept up too far, and Leeds finished on 134/5 — five runs short of the target. Trent Rockets Women held on to win by 5 runs and pick up the points in the group-stage standings.
stories.why_it_matters: Every group-stage win matters for seeding into The Hundred's playoffs, and a narrow finish like this — decided by just 5 runs — usually swings on a handful of key overs, exactly the kind of tight finish the tournament format is designed to produce.
stories.ripple_effects: The result nudges Trent Rockets Women up the group table and dents Sunrisers Leeds Women's playoff hopes with the group stage nearing its end. It also keeps Sutherland's strong individual form in the spotlight even in a losing effort.
stories.why_now: This was simply today's scheduled Match 17 in The Hundred's ongoing 2026 group stage.
stories.watch_next: Watch The Hundred's group table over the final matches to see which four women's teams qualify for the playoffs.

key_terms.definition: An English cricket competition where each team faces 100 balls per innings (instead of the 120 balls of a normal T20), designed to be shorter and simpler for new fans to follow.

stories.the_lesson: In short-format cricket, a handful of runs decide entire results — the shorter the format, the less room there is for a team to recover from a slow passage of play.

stories.title: West Indies win the toss and bat first in the series-deciding 2nd Test against Pakistan
key_points: West Indies won the toss and **chose to bat first** at Queen's Park Oval, Port of Spain.
West Indies lead the two-match series **1-0** after winning the first Test by **90 runs**.
Pakistan, missing usual captain Shan Masood from the leadership role, are led by **Babar Azam** for this series decider.
Pakistan's XI includes **Azan Awais** and **Abdullah Shafique** both in the top order as the batting group is reshuffled.
A West Indies win completes a **series sweep**; Pakistan must win outright to level it.
stories.background: Pakistan arrived in the Caribbean already under pressure, having lost the first Test of this two-match series by **90 runs** on July 25 — a defeat built on a five-wicket haul from West Indies quick **Jayden Seales** and a lone fighting fifty from Babar Azam that wasn't enough. That defeat saw the captaincy handed to **Babar Azam** instead of Shan Masood for this decider. West Indies, under **Roston Chase**, sense a rare chance to complete a clean sweep of Pakistan at home.
stories.what_happened: At the toss for the second and final Test in Port of Spain, Pakistan's Babar Azam lost the call and West Indies opted to **bat first** — a decision that puts early pressure on Pakistan's bowling attack, led by Mohammad Ali and Sajid Khan, against a home side already 1-0 up. Pakistan's batting order shows Azan Awais opening alongside Imam-ul-Haq, with Abdullah Shafique also in the XI, reflecting the uncertainty in Pakistan's top order after the first-Test loss. West Indies field their settled top order of Tagenarine Chanderpaul, Brandon King, and Kavem Hodge in front of captain Roston Chase.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a **series decider**: lose it, and Pakistan suffer a Test series defeat in the Caribbean; win it, and West Indies complete a rare clean sweep over a major touring side. For Babar Azam, leading the side in place of Masood, the result will shape the conversation about Pakistan's Test captaincy going forward.
stories.ripple_effects: A West Indies win would be a significant confidence boost for a side that has struggled for consistency in Test cricket in recent years, and would sharpen scrutiny on Pakistan's batting depth and captaincy choices ahead of their next assignments. A Pakistan win would keep the series alive and validate the Babar-over-Masood captaincy call.
stories.why_now: This is simply the start of play in the day-by-day Test, following directly from the first Test's result on July 25.
stories.watch_next: Watch how West Indies' innings unfolds on Day 1 — a big total puts Pakistan under serious pressure to save the series.

key_terms.definition: A coin flip before a cricket match where the winning captain decides whether their team bats or bowls first — a decision that can shape the whole match depending on pitch and weather conditions.

stories.the_lesson: In multi-match series, losing the opening game doesn't just cost points — it can cost the losing captain their job for the very next match, since selectors often read a defeat as a referendum on leadership, not just form.
